claims.value: Fwd (A_Prolif_Fwd): SILAC heavy = 22000 Pa, SILAC light = 400 Pa; Rev (B_Prolif_Rev): SILAC heavy = 400 Pa, SILAC light = 22000 Pa
claims.evidence: Paper: "SILAC-labeled ECs were cultured on PAGs of differing matrix stiffness (physiological, 400 Pa, and pathological, 22,000 Pa) for 24 h"; "forward and reverse experiments, where labeling conditions were swapped". Dataset EV1 column "22/0.4 KPa Fwd (log2)" with Intensity H > L for stiffness-up UBE2C; Appendix: "The reported H/L ratio was inverted in ... reverse SILAC labeling experiments", so Fwd H/L = 22/0.4 and Rev H/L = 0.4/22. EV1 Fwd/Rev columns equal MaxQuant experiments A_Prolif_Fwd/B_Prolif_Rev intensities exactly (ev1_match). Data check: CYR61/CCN1 (paper: highly induced by stiffness) normalized H/L = 2.33 in A_Prolif_Fwd and 0.58 in B_Prolif_Rev; CDH2 2.12 / 0.55.

claims.value: SILAC light = study sample; SILAC heavy = SILAC-HUVEC standard
claims.evidence: Paper/PRIDE: "a heavy SILAC-HUVEC standard was mixed at a 1:1 ratio with each of the lysates from the non-labeled samples (triplicates for each condition)". MaxQuant Labels1 = Arg10;Lys8. Dataset EV3 "Ratio siCCN 1 /STD", EV1 "Ratio 4h/SILAC standard_1" = inverted H/L. Data check: CYR61 normalized H/L 5.4/7.2/8.8 in siCCN 1-3 vs 1.1/1.1/1.8 in CTL 1-3 (knock-down lowers the light channel); GAPDH ~0.9-1.0.

claims.value: reference on the 60 heavy-standard rows (rows 74,76,78,80,82,84 (siCCN1 heavy standard) and 91-96,103-108,115-120,127-132,139-144,151-156,163-168,175-180,187-192 (Matrigel heavy standard)); study sample on the other 132 rows (both stiffness channels, rows 1-72, and every spike-in light row)
claims.evidence: Paper/PRIDE: "a heavy SILAC-HUVEC standard was mixed at a 1:1 ratio with each of the lysates from the non-labeled samples"; the standard is the common reference for the ratio-of-ratios ("In SILAC spike-in experiments the ratio of ratios between experimental conditions was calculated"). OLS4: PRIDE:0000899 "reference" (not obsolete), ancestors PRIDE:0000898 multiplex sample -> PRIDE:0000895 sample type, so it is within the column's permitted subtree; PRIDE:0001013 "study sample" is a direct child of PRIDE:0000895. Same light = study sample / heavy = reference pattern as campaign precedents PXD009868, PXD030422, PXD012113.

claims.value: stiffness Fwd = 1, Rev = 2 within each stiffness; siCTL/siCCN1 1-3; Matrigel 1-3 per time point; heavy standard aliquots = 1
claims.evidence: Fwd and Rev are independent label-swap cultures (paper); siCCN1 and Matrigel "triplicates for each condition", numbered as in MaxQuant experiments CTL 1-3 / siCCN 1-3 / 4h_1-3 etc. Rule 3: numbering restarts per factor group. Heavy standard rows keep biological replicate 1 rather than pooled: the paper describes one standard per experiment ("a heavy SILAC-HUVEC standard"), i.e. a single heavy-labelled HUVEC preparation aliquoted into every mixture, not a mixture of distinct study samples or cell lines (the template reserves pooled for pooled reference samples; donor pooling of the HUVECs themselves is already carried by characteristics[pooled sample] = pooled on every row). Its aliquots are distinguished by source name.
Human umbilical vein endothelial cells; PRIDE organisms NEWT:9606; searched against human UniProt. NCBITaxon:9606 verified.
Paper Methods: "Human umbilical vein endothelial cells were isolated from freshly collected umbilical cords". UBERON:0002066 umbilical vein verified.
HUVECs (paper); PRIDE organismParts CL:0000071 blood vessel endothelial cell (the more specific CL:0002618 endothelial cell of umbilical vein verified in OLS).

Paper Methods: "Cells from 3 to 5 cords were pooled." (Patella et al. 2015, the lab's Matrigel study, likewise: "HUVECs isolated from 2-5 umbilical cords were pooled"). Every row is HUVEC material from a multi-donor pool.
Primary HUVECs isolated in-house from umbilical cords and used up to passage six (paper Methods) - primary cells, not an established cell line.

limitations: PARTIAL SCOPE: 96 of 132 deposited .raw files annotated. Excluded (rule 7): the 36 files 20140715_Elite_StRe_STIFF_Prot_MitoC_Fwd_C1-C18 and _MitoC_Rev_D1-D18 (MaxQuant experiments C_MitoC_Fwd, D_MitoC_Rev in txtstiffness.zip). Neither the paper, its Appendix, Datasets EV1-3, the review process file, the PRIDE protocol nor any other Europe PMC record citing PXD003316 describes this arm: the treatment behind "MitoC" (presumably mitomycin C, never stated) and the stiffness per SILAC channel are undocumented. The full list is in the report and BLOCKED.md.

Raw headers were read for 9 of 96 annotated files (techsdrf not installed); the per-arm fragmentation settings were constant in every sampled file and match the Appendix (rCID for stiffness, HCD for siCCN1/Matrigel).
Appendix says HCD top ten; the stiffness rCID method is Top15 (raw header). Not encoded in a column.
comment[cleavage agent details] records the digestion enzyme Trypsin (rule 2); the MaxQuant search rule was Trypsin/P (MS:1001313).

comment[alkylation reagent] is not available: the paper and PRIDE give only DTT reduction; carbamidomethyl (C) is fixed in all three searches, so an alkylation step is implied but its reagent is unstated (PRIDE identifiedPTM MOD:00397 "iodoacetamide derivatized residue" describes the search modification, not a reagent statement).

Composition of the heavy SILAC-HUVEC standard (culture condition, whether siCCN1 and Matrigel experiments used the same preparation) is not described; its growth condition / genetic modification / sampling time are not available and its factor values not applicable; it is marked characteristics[sample type] = reference (PRIDE:0000899). Under convert-openms both experiments' standards (60 files) share the condition "not applicable|not applicable|not applicable" by design: they are reference channels, not a compared group, and source names keep the two experiments' standards apart.

Review round 1 (external) listed 66 heavy-standard rows; the SDRF has 60 (siCCN1 6 + Matrigel 54, matching the reviewer's own row ranges); sample type = reference was applied to exactly those 60 rows and study sample to the other 132.
Donor age, sex, ancestry and disease status are not available (HUVECs pooled from 3-5 anonymous umbilical cords); developmental stage left out rather than inferred from "umbilical cord".
siCCN1 culture/transfection duration before lysis is not stated: sampling time not available on those rows.

characteristics[growth condition] and characteristics[genetic modification] are custom columns (not licensed by ms-proteomics/human; allowed by spec "Extending Templates", campaign rule 15) with free-text values.

The PRIDE sample protocol conflates two experiments ("HUVECs silenced for CCN1 and cultured on Matrigel"); the paper ("For the proteome of HUVECs silenced for CCN1 and those cultured on Matrigel") and Dataset EV3 ("cultured on plastic dish") show siCCN1 on plastic and Matrigel as a separate experiment; the paper was followed.
The 30 h Matrigel samples are deposited and searched but not used in the paper (which compares 4 h vs 22 h); annotated from file and MaxQuant experiment names.

PRIDE data-processing text says MaxQuant 1.3.6.0 was used for a "contact inhibited" dataset; no such runs are in this deposit (the confluence 1d/4d ratios in Dataset EV1 come from Patella et al. 2016).
ms-proteomics is declared at v1.2.0 (upstream bigbio/sdrf-templates 7da1747 templates.yaml latest); the spec submodule's nested templates copy is older.
Review not performed by the producer: status REVIEW_PENDING_EXTERNAL (external sdrf-adversarial-review hand-off named in the request).
